checks: The accepted radial-cut hypotheses hold: P is lattice complete, the original positive fibers satisfy the anchored inclusions, each selected slope is continuous and affine in the base RHS, and each jointly continuous nonnegative convex field is defined on the common canonical hull. The construction leaves the finite positive integer census and projection unchanged, in the relative ambient space.

The radial theorem gives the maximum field value over the old tight contacts at each regular boundary point. The forced-row selection makes these exactly the universal contacts. Its cap selector distinguishes whole/inside-support and pure-base equality from outside-support or disjoint interior, and uses the strict bit in proper cuts, including the one-dimensional endpoint convention.

Every feasible slope retains every forced row; the field-wise maximum is therefore at least the one displayed, and integrating with nonnegative selectors orders the total and each individual cap loss. This does not order their signed difference.

Finite projection averages have decreasing contact sets with forced-set intersection. Finiteness of the source list makes their maximum speeds decrease to the exact one at each regular boundary point. The fixed field bound and finite surface measure give dominated convergence for each cap and simultaneously for any finite list. No uniform bound on the slopes as the index increases is needed.

dependencies.hypotheses: Use the continuous exact forced-contact selection for each marked base, and its decreasing finite-average contact sets. Anchored compatibility at each source is part of the hypotheses. Same-wave parent pending graph admission.

Apply its actual convex radial-loss theorem on the lattice-complete canonical hull with continuous affine-in-base majorants and the nonnegative jointly continuous convex fields. It supplies the proper/supporting/pure-base selector and relative-space result.

overlap.comparison: It establishes loss formulas for each given feasible continuous slope. It does not construct the minimal contact choice or compare finite averages to that choice.

readability: If the finite source list is empty, the unchanged family has identically zero losses, as follows directly from the definition.
review_method: Independent mathematical proof review of the frozen normalized candidate
summary: Selecting exactly the forced rows minimizes each nonnegative first-loss functional for fixed fields.
